title: Semantic HTML
description: Understanding semantic elements to create meaningful and accessible web pages.

flashcards.question: What is Semantic HTML?
flashcards.answer: HTML that uses meaningful tags to clearly describe the content's purpose and structure.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of the <nav> element?
flashcards.answer: To define a section containing navigation links.

flashcards.question: How does the <article> tag differ from <section>?
flashcards.answer: <article> represents a self-contained piece of content; <section> is a thematic grouping of content.

flashcards.question: Why should you use semantic elements instead of generic <div>?
flashcards.answer: They improve accessibility, SEO, and code readability by clearly defining content roles.

flashcards.question: What semantic element is used to contain the main content of a document?
What element is typically used to contain sidebars or tangential content?
Which semantic element is used to define the footer of a document or section?
Can semantic elements contain other semantic elements?
flashcards.answer: Yes, semantic elements can be nested as needed.

flashcards.question: How do semantic elements help screen readers?
flashcards.answer: They provide meaningful landmarks to help users navigate content easily.
